newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks finish weaker, ignore Dow rally.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks finish weaker, ignore Dow rally.

text.p: Toronto stocks finished softer on Friday, ignoring a strong rally on Wall Street as investors grabbed profits in Canada's biggest stock market.
The TSE 300 Composite Index fell 4.37 points to close at 5917.80 in heavy turnover of 101 million shares worth C$1.58 billion ($1.17 billion).
Declining stocks outnumbered advances 495 to 471, with 277 issues unchanged.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average soared 53 points.
"New York bubbles ahead, but we're seeing some end of the week profit-taking," said Fred Ketchen, director of equity trading for ScotiaMcLeod Inc.
Communications and transportation led nine of Toronto's 14 sub-indices lower. There were modest gains in consumer products, energy and financial services.
Ketchen said investors would be watching Canada's big six banks next week when they start reporting year-end results.
Bank stocks have soared to all-time highs and powered the TSE to new heights since September.
"Next week there should be some interesting developments because on Tuesday the Bank of Montreal starts off with its earnings," Ketchen said.
* Bre-X Minerals Ltd. rose 0.20 to 23.90 on 1.8 million shares. Analysts on Friday dismissed threats of another lawsuit over Bre-X's ownership of a rich Indonesian gold deposit.

* Anvil Range Mining Corp. topped most actives, sinking 0.83 to 1.47 on 3.2 million shares. Earlier in the session, Anvil sank to a 52-week low of 1.40. The company shut its operations earlier this week.
* Laidlaw Inc. class B depressed the transportation group, falling 0.25 to 16.05 on 1.5 million shares.
* Royal Bank of Canada was the most-active bank issue, climbing 0.25 to 46.65 on 1.2 million shares.
